subject: Payment parachute & VAT reserve arrangement for CardioPulse — proposal
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena@cardiopulse.it>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: Payment terms & VAT handling while we migrate entity

Hi Sofia,

Quick note from AP on our upcoming production onboarding (RDW-9482). We’re in the middle of an internal entity migration — most invoices for Q4 will need to be routed from CardioPulse Italy (VAT ID IT12345678) to the new German sub (CardioPulse GmbH) for cross-border services. That means our treasury is asking for a temporary extension to Net45 for the first three invoices and a small credit buffer while we complete the migration.

Specific asks: 
- Can Redwood accept Net45 for the first three invoices (then revert to Net30)?
- A temporary rolling credit cushion of EUR 200,000 during the migration window.
- A 10% VAT reserve on each invoice that we will reconcile monthly once VAT registration is confirmed.

If you can send a short proposal (invoice schedule + any evidence you need from our side) we can get legal/finance to sign off faster.

Thanks,
Elena
Accounts Payable | CardioPulse S.p.A.
attachments: none
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 10:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Payment terms & VAT handling while we migrate entity

Hi Elena — thanks for the heads up and congrats on the migration. We can absolutely put together an operational-friendly plan so your teams don’t block the onboarding. High-level proposal below; I’ve attached a short PDF with the invoice schedule and two optional guardrails.

Proposal (summary):
- Temporary Net45 for the first three invoices tied to the migration window (we’ll auto-revert to your standard Net30 thereafter).
- Rolling credit corridor: Redwood can provision a dynamic cushion of EUR 250,000 tied to the active invoice balance (not an upfront line). The corridor will be reviewed after two consecutive on-time payments.
- 10% VAT reserve: Redwood will apply a 10% holdback on each invoice and issue a monthly reconciliation statement. When CardioPulse provides VAT registration evidence for the invoicing entity (VAT cert or local tax registration), we will release holds against that entity’s invoices.
- Escrow option: For the first two invoices you can elect to route payment to an escrow account (we’ll provide instructions) — Redwood will release against production KPIs or standard acceptance.

Attachments: 20261113-redwood-invoice-schedule-proposal.pdf (contains the invoice calendar, holdback accounting example, and the quick DocuSign routing for the escrow addendum).

Marissa — can you confirm finance is comfortable with the EUR 250k rolling cushion and the holdback accounting flow? Rishi — FYI from a risk/tax perspective since they’re moving entities across borders.

Elena, if this looks reasonable I’ll put a 1-page amendment into DocuSign and include the quick steps you need to provide VAT evidence.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
sofia@redwood.com | +44 20 5555 0123

Thanks Sofia — that proposal is helpful and I’ve flagged it to treasury. A few follow-ups from our side: 
1) The EUR 250k corridor is reasonable, but treasury prefers a capped bridge (EUR 200k) until we provide the German VAT cert (expected in ~3 weeks). Can the corridor be staged?
2) For the 10% VAT reserve: can Redwood accept our VAT certificate as PDF (we’ll attach) and then apply releases retroactively to invoices once certificate is validated?
3) On the escrow option: we’d prefer escrow for only the onboarding/integration invoice while the first production week is live.

We’ll attach the Italian VAT cert now and the German cert once issued. If you can send the DocuSign amendment with the two options (staged credit corridor or escrow-first) we can route quickly.

Regards,
Elena

Thanks for the summary, Sofia. Finance reviewed the ask and we can proceed with a staged credit corridor, subject to these conditions: 
- Staged corridor: approve EUR 200,000 immediately (effective day one). Increase to EUR 250,000 once CardioPulse provides validated German VAT registration for the billing entity (we will validate via local registry).
- Escrow: we will accept the escrow routing for the onboarding invoice for up to 14 days post-live. Release conditions: production live + 7-day health check (no severity P1 incidents). If an incident occurs, funds release will be paused and reconciled against remediation milestones.
- Holdback accounting: Redwood will apply the 10% VAT reserve as a line-item hold on each invoice and maintain a monthly reconciliation ledger. Upon validation of VAT evidence, releases will be applied retroactively and credited on the next invoice.

Operational notes:
- Please use the attached sample escrow addendum and the staged-corridor clause I’ve redlined in the DocuSign template.
- Legal will need to sign the 1-page amendment. I’ll prep DocuSign once Sofia confirms the final language.

Approved by: Marissa Cole, Head of Finance (payments & revenue ops)
